about: Coach-facing wording Christian has APPROVED for parts of a game the renderer otherwise cannot say: primary-event conditions (register V4-V6) and information rules (V16-V22), and later the modifier criterion and termination (V8c, V8d). His order of 14 October 2026, Step 4 component 3: 'Enable accurate coach-facing communication of scoring conditions and information rules, using approved language.' An entry is used only when it carries approvedBy with who, a date, his words verbatim and the communication standard it was reviewed under; the loader ignores any other entry and a data test fails it. Wording is data, so no sport term enters universal code. Starts EMPTY on 14 October 2026: until he approves a sentence, every such field is withheld and the activity is refused at communication rather than paraphrased. The first entry, A01-W1, was added 18 October 2026 (stage M5): his own sentence for the build-out scoring rule, reply filed 19 October 2026, item 1. A01-W2 and A01-W3 were added 18 October 2026 (design step L14): his reply filed 20 October 2026, item 1 (the pressing team's regain score, our draft approved as written) and item 2 (the building team's scoring eligibility, in his own simplified wording). His approval covers these sentences only: "I understand that the remaining coach-facing sentences are still drafts, so this approval applies specifically to the two scoring statements, not yet to the entire activity."

entries.sentence: Building team: Score by carrying the ball beyond the marked line or passing to a teammate who receives it under control beyond the line. The progression must begin with the goalkeeper's build-out and occur before the building team loses possession. Uncontrolled clearances do not score.

approvedBy.quote:
1. Build-out scoring condition — Approved with revised wording
I'd like to simplify the coach-facing wording while preserving the four conditions established in the knowledge.
Suggested wording:
"Building team: Score by carrying the ball beyond the marked line or passing to a teammate who receives it under control beyond the line. The progression must begin with the goalkeeper's build-out and occur before the building team loses possession. Uncontrolled clearances do not score."
A longer pass received under control remains a valid solution.
The important distinction is that the building team's scoring opportunity applies only during an active build-out episode.
approvedBy.ccs: Coach Communication Standard RC2: his own revision of our draft condition sentence, section 4 of our email of 18 October 2026 ("The wording that needs your approval"), which put every sentence to him as a draft

entries.note: Added 18 October 2026 (stage M5, design step L13); his reply filed 19 October 2026, item 1. One sentence for the build-out scoring rule, said once: the building role's credit bound (B8 = BUILD_OUT_EPISODE, his item 1 and item 3 C, A01-R1-B8-1) and the four conditions his item 1 preserves (origin RPC-001-18.a, progression 18.c, control 18.f, exclusion 19.a), each covered with its exact scope (V3). The match values are the game's own, copied from A01 as the checked pathway builds it at 12 and 11 players, identical in both blocks (measured). The 18.a asAuthored text is the wording he approved on 18 October 2026, item 4 ("I acknowledge and approve your proposed wording": our proposal, approved by him, so not an unapproved gloss of ours), which names both arms of the origin (the goalkeeper, or a controlled defensive restart). His 19 October sentence names only the goalkeeper. OUR INFERRED READING: he narrowed his own wording to the one arm this realization builds, after section 4 of our email of 18 October 2026 told him that every build-out in this activity starts with the goalkeeper and the engine cannot yet build the controlled-defensive-restart arm; a test pins that no episode starter of A01 carries a restart kind, so the arm his sentence leaves unnamed cannot occur. The suffixes after ' - ' on the 18.c, 18.f and 19.a asAuthored texts are our glosses, matched here as data only. If any of these values changes, the entry stops matching, the fields are withheld again and A01 is refused at communication (a safe failure).

approvedBy.quote:
1. Pressing team's regain score — Approved as written.

"The pressing team also scores by winning the ball inside that zone, provided it genuinely establishes possession; a contested touch, deflection or loose ball does not count."

This preserves the intended incentive for controlled high regains without requiring an additional pass or dribble.
approvedBy.ccs: Coach Communication Standard RC2: our draft, sentence 1 of our email of 19 October 2026 ("Play Out from the Back - one sentence to approve, then the activity is served"), approved by him as written in his reply filed 20 October 2026, item 1

entries.note: Added 18 October 2026 (design step L14); his reply filed 20 October 2026, item 1. One sentence for the pressing team's regain score, said once: the four fields of the one element that also counts as the primary event for the team holding the pressing role (A01-R1-V27-1 with V29-1, V30-1 and V31-1; his reply filed 19 October 2026, item 2), located by its team. Each field is a thing the sentence says: 'The pressing team' (V28, the team), 'winning the ball' (V29, an in-play change of possession, never a restart awarded to it: OUR READING on A01-R1-V29-1), 'provided it genuinely establishes possession' (V30, his item-2 words) and 'a contested touch, deflection or loose ball does not count' (V31, his item-2 words; the match value keeps the comma of his 19 October ruling, the sentence the punctuation he approved on 20 October). 'that zone' is the target the pressing team attacks, which the element reads through its own team and which the pressing team's sentence names just before it (render-concrete-game.ts scoringInRoleOrder); the target is no field of this element, so nothing about it is covered here. The match values are the game's own, copied from A01-R1 as the checked pathway builds it at 12 and 11 players, identical in both blocks (measured). If any of these values changes, the entry stops matching, the four fields are withheld again and A01 is refused at communication (a safe failure).

equals.asAuthored: A restart, taken by the goalkeeper or as a controlled defensive restart, that begins a build-out episode.

entries.sentence: If the building team loses possession or plays the ball out, it cannot score again until the next goalkeeper restart.

approvedBy.quote:
2. Building team's scoring eligibility — Include, with simplified wording.

"If the building team loses possession or plays the ball out, it cannot score again until the next goalkeeper restart."

I think this clarification is useful because play continues after turnovers. Coaches should understand that regaining possession does not restore the original build-out scoring opportunity.
approvedBy.ccs: Coach Communication Standard RC2: his own simplified wording, replacing our draft, sentence 2 of our email of 19 October 2026 ("Play Out from the Back - one sentence to approve, then the activity is served"), in his reply filed 20 October 2026, item 2

entries.note: Added 18 October 2026 (design step L14); his reply filed 20 October 2026, item 2, in HIS wording, which replaces our draft. One sentence for the building team's scoring eligibility, said once, for his reply filed 19 October 2026, item 4 (the scoring instructions must make clear that continuing to attack does not restore the building team's eligibility). It covers what the sentence says and nothing more: the building role's credit bound (B8 = BUILD_OUT_EPISODE, A01-R1-B8-1: its holder scores only inside a build-out episode, which ends when it loses possession - the change of possession, GF2-07.a - or plays the ball out - the restarts after it, A01-R1-T1-5 and T1-7, which A01-R1-T7-3 makes begin another episode - and which only a goalkeeper restart begins, A01-R1-T1-1..3), and the origin condition that names that restart (RPC-001-18.a: its type, its exact scope and its referents, the same values as A01-W1, whose note explains the goalkeeper-only reading of the two arms; a test pins that no episode starter of A01 carries a restart kind). Those episode-ending transitions are not fields an entry can cover (the renderer says them in its own How it works sentences); what this sentence says about them is the B8 episode they end, checked by GA-EPISODE-REACHABLE clauses 4 and 5. The progression, control and exclusion conditions are NOT covered: this sentence does not say them. Two entries covering one field (MEASURED, approved-wording.unit.ts and first-activity-end-to-end.unit.ts): each located entry is said once where all its own covers hold, independently of the other, citing the fields it covers; a field is withheld only where no entry says it. So B8 and the origin's three fields are cited by A01-W1 and by A01-W3, and neither entry decides the other: without A01-W1 the three conditions only it covers are withheld (refused), and without A01-W3 the fields are still said by A01-W1, so a test pins that the served activity says this sentence once. Its place in How to score, straight after A01-W1, follows from citing the building role's bound (render-concrete-game.ts scoringInRoleOrder, then table order). If any of these values changes, the entry stops matching (a safe failure for these fields, which A01-W1 also says).

templateShape.note: Added 17 October 2026 (stage M4) for his reply filed 19 October 2026, item 4. approvedTemplateSentences.renders: A game whose transition keyed on a change of possession continues play, with one objective per team: the first part cites each such transition's play state and selector, the second the objectives' team and the targets' noun (render-concrete-game.ts, 'How it works'). The second part is said only where the two objectives name different teams; targetNoun is the referenced regions' one noun, and 'line' where they name no other.

approvedBy.quote: I approve both of your proposed revisions: … Use: "When possession changes, play carries on without a stoppage, and each team keeps attacking the same zone." For the second sentence, please ensure the surrounding scoring instructions make clear that continuing to attack does not automatically restore the building team's eligibility to score.
